title: Hair Transplant in Istanbul: Complete Guide for International Patients
desc: Everything you need to know before booking — costs, clinic standards, techniques, and what to expect.
body:
Why Istanbul?

Istanbul has become the global capital of hair restoration, treating over 1 million patients annually from across Europe, the Middle East, and beyond. World-class surgeons, state-of-the-art clinics, and costs 60–70% lower than the UK or US make it an obvious choice.

Choosing a Clinic

Not all clinics are equal. Look for JCI-accredited facilities with qualified surgical teams — not technician-led procedures. Lucera partners exclusively with clinics that meet international standards.

title: Month by Month: What to Expect After Your Hair Transplant
desc: A realistic timeline covering shock loss, new growth, and when you'll see final results.
body:
Weeks 1–2

The transplanted area will be tender and scabbed. Sleep upright, avoid direct water pressure, and follow your aftercare kit instructions carefully.

Weeks 3–6: Shock Loss

Most transplanted hairs will shed. This is completely normal — the follicles remain alive beneath the surface.

Months 3–6: Early Growth

Fine new hairs begin to emerge. They may look thin at first — this is expected.

Months 9–18: Full Results

Hair thickens and matures. Final results are typically visible at 12–18 months.

title: FUE vs DHI: Which Technique Is Right for Your Hair Loss?
desc: The key differences explained — and how to know which approach suits your specific pattern.
body:
FUE (Follicular Unit Extraction)

Individual follicles are extracted from the donor area and implanted into incisions made in the recipient area. Highly versatile and suitable for most hair loss patterns.

DHI (Direct Hair Implantation)

Uses a specialised Choi pen to extract and implant in one step, without pre-made incisions. Offers precise control over angle and direction — ideal for frontal hairline work.

Which Is Right for You?

Your surgeon will assess your donor density, loss pattern, and desired outcome to recommend the best approach. Many procedures combine both techniques.
